messages:
nate: Quick RFC follow-up: proposal for an "edge-led degrade contract". Goal: let edges make very fast decisions to shed/degrade while keeping client semantics clear. Modes: SHED (HTTP 503 + code), TRUNCATE (stream trailer + marker), FALLBACK (redirect to cheaper model). Thoughts?

anya: +1. main worry is flappy edges disagreeing. we need a short "policy-epoch" in headers so downstreams can detect version changes.

kevin: agree on epoch. also: retries. do not allow transparent retries for non-idempotent routes. retries must carry original-degrade-epoch and a retry-attempt header.

 sophia: client visibility: propose `X-Rw-Degrade: TRUNCATE;code=DEGRADE_TRUNCATED;epoch=7`. Client SDKs show "partial result" UI. Add trace tag `rw.degrade=true`.

nate: good. ops note: when TRUNCATE happens emit a synthetic billing marker (0-cost) so billing doesn't bill tokens after the truncate point. avoids customer surprise.

kevin: config sketch: `route:/v1/generate priority:medium degrade:
  - p95_queue_ms: 200 -> TRUNCATE
  - p99_queue_ms: 900 -> SHED`

anya: rollout: control-plane pushes rollout_id+epoch. edges accept signed policies. canary sequence by region -> tenant-size.

sre-bot: staged test (2026-03-25) inject p99 latency, observed TRUNCATE on /v1/generate for tenant acme-inc, epoch=7 :rocket:

nate: i'll draft RFC follow-up with enums (`INGRESS_SHED`, `DEGRADE_TRUNCATED`, `FALLBACK_REDIRECT`) and a short test plan. thanks.
